content:
Here's an example of a spam message someone might receive on an online platform:

---

**From: CryptoKing_Mike99**

"Hey there! 👋 I noticed your profile and you seem like a smart person. I wanted to share an AMAZING opportunity with you!!! 

My team and I have developed a revolutionary crypto investment system that GUARANTEES 300% returns in just 7 days!!! 💰💰💰

I've already helped over 5,000 people become MILLIONAIRES this year alone. Don't miss out!

Just click this link to get started: [bit.ly/crypto-riches-now]

⏰ HURRY! Only 3 spots left at this price!
⏰ Offer ends in 1 HOUR!

DM me your email and phone number and I'll personally walk you through it. Also need a small $200 deposit to 'activate' your account - this is fully refundable (trust me!).

Don't tell anyone about this - it's our little secret! 🤫

Reply 'YES' to claim your spot!"

---

This example demonstrates several common spam red flags:
- Unsolicited contact from a stranger
- Unrealistic promises ("guaranteed 300% returns")
- High-pressure tactics ("only 3 spots left," "ends in 1 hour")
- Requests for personal information
- Suspicious shortened links
- Upfront payment requirements
- Excessive emojis and capitalization
- Urging secrecy

This kind of example can be useful for training spam filters, educating users about scams, or creating awareness content about online safety.
